name: Sell beat leases and exclusives on BeatStars / Airbit
summary: Produce instrumentals and sell non-exclusive leases (MP3/WAV/stems) and exclusive rights to rappers and singers via beat stores.
howItWorks: You produce instrumentals in popular genres (trap, drill, afrobeats, R&B) and list them on a beat store with tiered license contracts: cheap non-exclusive leases with stream caps, pricier stem/unlimited leases, and exclusive buyouts (the same mechanic covers 'ghost production' full-rights sales to DJs). Artists pay because they need affordable, ready-made production. Traffic comes from the marketplace search plus YouTube 'type beat' uploads that link to the store. Each beat can be leased many times until sold exclusively.

payout.minimumPayout: $0: direct store sales land in your own PayPal/Stripe; Airbit marketplace earnings have no minimum
payout.frequency: per sale (BeatStars, Airbit personal stores); monthly for Airbit marketplace
payout.notes: Verified (help centers, Nov 2026): BeatStars takes 0% of beat sales and funds go straight to the seller's connected PayPal/Stripe; a 12% Marketplace service fee is added to the buyer's price (sellers may opt to cover it), not charged on Pro Page/Blaze sales. Uploading and selling on BeatStars requires a paid Starter/Growth/Professional plan (pricing page showed Starter at $19.99/year during a promotion; free accounts are capped at 10 tracks). Airbit has a free account and Platinum ($19.99/mo or $7.99/mo billed annually); personal stores are zero-commission and pay instantly via PayPal/Stripe; marketplace earnings are paid on the last working day of the following month via Tipalti with no minimum threshold. Airbit's marketplace commission rate is not published. Airbit Content ID (Platinum only) pays 80%.

legality.notes: Selling licenses to your own compositions is legal everywhere; income is taxable. Beats using uncleared samples or AI output without rights cannot be licensed.
complianceRequirements: own or clear every sample/loop used
register works with PRO/publishing admin if desired

availability.notes: Both platforms accept sellers worldwide; direct sales need a PayPal or Stripe account in the seller's country, and Airbit marketplace payouts go via Tipalti (PayPal, ACH, wire, check). PayPal receiving is limited in a few reference countries (e.g. Bangladesh, Libya, Iraq), and Stripe is unavailable in many African and South Asian countries, so Airbit's Tipalti wire option may be the only route there. Zero-capital route is Airbit's free account; BeatStars needs a paid plan (about $20/year at promo pricing).

automationPlan: Auto-generate titles, tags and 'type beat' descriptions with an LLM
Batch-render tagged MP3 previews, WAVs and stem zips
Scheduled YouTube type-beat uploads via API linking to store
Contract PDFs generated by the platform automatically
fullCycle: Produce and upload beats with license tiers
risks: Extremely saturated market; most beats never sell
Platform fee/plan changes (BeatStars now requires a paid plan to sell)
evidence: BeatStars' help center states it takes 0% of beat sales and pays sellers directly via PayPal/Stripe; Airbit's site reports $50M+ earned by producers and documents monthly Tipalti marketplace payouts with no minimum.

tools: free DAW (Cakewalk, Waveform Free, BandLab) or FL Studio if owned

unitEconomics.notes: Basic leases sell for about $20-50, premium/unlimited $100-200, exclusives $300+. BeatStars takes 0% from the seller (12% marketplace fee is charged to buyers); cost is PayPal/Stripe processing. Hours amortise production and promotion per sale.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurring $2/mo (startup cash not amortised). One lease a month covers the plan; most producers need 50-100 uploaded beats and months of type-beat uploads before the first sale.

marketConditions.notes: Millions of beats are listed; sales concentrate among producers with large YouTube type-beat channels and artist relationships. Licensed AI music generators since 2025 give independent artists near-free instrumentals, pressuring cheap leases. Failure modes: no traffic, beats that never sell, and sample-clearance disputes.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Use the standard ladder ($25-30 basic MP3 lease, $50-100 WAV/stems, $300+ exclusive) with bundle deals (buy 2 get 1) to win first buyers; raise prices once a beat or channel gets traction.
profitPath: Month 0: 20 beats, store, license templates (cost ~$20/yr plan)
Month 1-3: 2-3 type-beat uploads per week; first lease, $0-50
Month 3-6: 60+ beats, collaborations with small artists; $20-150/month
Month 6-12: focus on the genre that sells, email list; most stay under $100/month

name: Sample packs and synth presets on Splice, Loopmasters and Producer Loops
summary: Create royalty-free loops, one-shots, MIDI and synth presets and distribute them through sample-pack labels that pay per download or per sale.
howItWorks: You build themed packs (drums, vocal chops, Serum/Vital presets, MIDI progressions) and either apply as a provider/label on Splice, where subscribers spend credits per sound and creators are paid per download, or register as a vendor/label on stores such as Producer Loops (50% royalty) or pitch Loopmasters/ADSR, which sell whole packs and pay a royalty share. You can also sell packs directly on Gumroad/your own store. Producers pay because ready-made, cleared sounds save them time.

payout.minimumPayout: Producer Loops: £100 balance (smaller amounts roll over); Splice and Loopmasters: not published
payout.frequency: quarterly (Producer Loops from 1 Jan 2026); Splice/Loopmasters per label agreement
payout.notes: Verified from Producer Loops provider terms (register page): 50% royalty on the GBP list price after VAT and affiliate payouts; 50% pro-rata share of FL Cloud license fees (curated labels) and of an AI-training royalty pool; paid via PayPal or bank transfer within 30 days after quarter end, £100 minimum. Vendor registration is still linked from the site, so the earlier 410 on the old 'sell your samples' URL was just a moved page. Splice says creators are paid each time a sound is downloaded and has paid out over $25M in total, but does not publish its per-download rate. Loopmasters invites producers to contact info@loopmasters.com and publishes no split.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; you license your own recordings royalty-free. Must not contain uncleared third-party audio.
complianceRequirements: disclose AI generation where label requires

availability.notes: Producer Loops vendor registration is self-serve and pays by PayPal (bank transfer for UK providers); Splice and Loopmasters accept creators internationally, but only after curation. PayPal receiving is limited in a few reference countries (e.g. Bangladesh, Libya, Iraq); Payoneer/Wise or local alternatives may be needed.

automationPlan: Script batch export, naming, tempo/key tagging and demo rendering
LLM-generated pack descriptions and metadata
Automated preset rendering/previews from synth patch files
fullCycle: Apply to Splice/label or open own store
risks: Producer Loops now pays quarterly with a £100 minimum, so small sellers may wait several quarters
evidence: Splice reports paying sound creators over $25M since launching Splice Sounds; Producer Loops' provider terms publish a 50% royalty with quarterly PayPal/bank payouts.

tools: Gumroad or Payhip free tier for direct sales
skills: clean editing, naming and tagging of samples

unitEconomics.notes: Packs retail $10-50 (Producer Loops/Loopmasters); Producer Loops pays a 50% royalty (fee 50%). Splice per-download rates are unpublished. Hours amortise pack creation over expected sales. Splice royalty is estimated; Producer Loops' 50% royalty is confirmed on its provider terms.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash outlay; Producer Loops pays quarterly with a GBP 100 minimum, so cash can lag sales by 4-9 months.

marketConditions.notes: Established labels with distinctive genre packs and big producer names dominate Splice and the stores. Subscription models have lowered per-sound income, and AI sample generators add free supply in 2025-26. Failure modes: label rejection, packs that sell a handful of copies, piracy of direct-sold packs.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Give away a free mini-pack to build an email list, price the first full pack at $10-15 direct, and pitch labels only once you have a track record or a niche (e.g. specific regional genres).
profitPath: Month 0-1: produce a 150-300 sound pack and a free sampler (cost $0)
Month 2-4: direct sales plus vendor listing; $0-50/month
Month 4-8: second pack, label pitches; first quarterly royalty
Month 8-12: a back catalogue of 3-4 packs; most earn $20-100/month

name: Remote session musician, vocalist, mixing and mastering gigs (AirGigs, SoundBetter, Fiverr)
summary: Sell remote recording (instrument/vocal tracks), mixing and mastering to artists through music-specific freelance marketplaces.
howItWorks: You list productized services (e.g. 'mix up to 24 stems', 'session guitar track', 'female topline vocal', 'mastering per song') on AirGigs, SoundBetter and Fiverr's music categories. Clients upload stems or references, you deliver files, and the marketplace releases payment on completion. AI-assisted tools (stem separation, assistive mixing/mastering) cut turnaround, but the core value is human ears and performance.

payout.minimumPayout: AirGigs: no stated minimum; Fiverr $1 PayPal / $20 Payoneer bank
payout.notes: AirGigs: one-time $20 activation fee, 10-15% commission (min $8/order), 3-day clearing then daily PayPal withdrawals. Fiverr: 20% fee, 14-day clearance. SoundBetter (terms of use): clients fund jobs up front and funds are released when the client closes the job; the payment provider deducts a 'Platform Fee' that is shown in the proposal but not published as a percentage; Storefront sales carry a 10% commission plus a $9.99/month Storefront subscription; payouts run through a third-party processor (Stripe Connect named).

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; taxable service income. Work-for-hire / credit terms should be agreed in writing.
complianceRequirements: no use of client stems for other purposes

availability.notes: AirGigs pays via PayPal (Payoneer beta); Fiverr pays via Payoneer almost everywhere. PayPal receiving is limited in a few reference countries (e.g. Bangladesh, Libya, Iraq); Payoneer/Wise or local alternatives may be needed.

automationPlan: Templates for proposals and delivery notes
Automated stem prep, loudness metering and file packaging
AI-assisted first-pass mix/master then human refinement
evidence: AirGigs' help center documents its commission tiers and daily PayPal withdrawals, showing an active paid marketplace for session work.

tools: DAW and plugins already owned (or free: Reaper trial, free plugins)
skills: mixing/mastering or session performance at a professional level
fast file turnaround and revision handling
equipment: instrument or vocal mic for session work

unitEconomics.unit: per song (mix, master or session track)
unitEconomics.notes: Fiverr/AirGigs mixing gigs cluster at $30-150 per song, pro mixes $200-400+. Fee of 20% is Fiverr's (AirGigs 10-15%, SoundBetter varies). AirGigs confirmed: $20 one-time activation, 10-15% commission with an $8 minimum per order.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. Startup cash is the AirGigs activation; one gig recovers it.

marketConditions.notes: Independent artists keep buying mixes and session parts, and engineers with strong before/after demos and genre specialisation win repeat clients. AI mastering (LANDR, iZotope assistants) has pushed basic mastering below $20. Failure modes: race-to-bottom pricing and endless revisions. Fact-check: median month-12 net lowered from $250 to $70 so it agrees with the 30% profit likelihood (fewer than half of starters clear $100/month, so the median starter cannot).

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Start with a low-priced 'first mix' gig ($30-50) with 2 revisions to collect reviews, then tier by stem count and raise to $100+ per mix after 15-20 reviews.
profitPath: Month 0: demo reel and 3 gig listings (cost $20)
Month 1-2: first 2-4 orders, $100-200
Month 3-6: repeat clients and Fiverr level-up; $300-800/month
Month 6-12: higher tiers and direct clients; $500-2,000/month for active sellers

name: Bandcamp direct-to-fan sales of music, merch and subscriptions
summary: Sell albums, tracks, digital extras and fan subscriptions directly to listeners on Bandcamp, which keeps a 10-15% revenue share.
howItWorks: You upload releases with name-your-price or fixed pricing, add bonus digital items and optional fan subscriptions, and drive fans to the page from social media, mailing lists and Bandcamp's own discovery. Fans pay because they want to support artists directly and own downloads. Bandcamp Fridays (when Bandcamp waives its share) concentrate fan spending. Physical merch is possible but involves shipping.

payout.minimumPayout: $0 (no minimum stated; PayPal charges a 1% payout fee capped at $1)
payout.frequency: per sale (default) or monthly on the 1st
payout.notes: Verified (Bandcamp help center): 15% share on digital (10% after $5,000 in trailing 12-month sales), 10% on physical, plus payment-processing fees, all deducted at the time of sale. Payouts go to the seller's connected PayPal 24-48 hours after processing (high-value orders may be reviewed for up to 14 days), or in bulk on the 1st of each month. Tax info is required after $5,000 in calendar-year sales. Bandcamp Fridays (Bandcamp waives its share) continue through 2026; the remaining dates are Nov 6 and Dec 4, 2026.

legality.notes: Selling your own music is legal everywhere; taxable. Covers require mechanical licenses for sales in some jurisdictions.
complianceRequirements: own the masters/compositions or license covers
sales tax/VAT handled per Bandcamp policy

availability.notes: Bandcamp artist accounts are open internationally, but payouts go only to PayPal, which cannot receive funds in a few reference countries (e.g. Bangladesh, Libya, Iraq). Physical merch adds shipping.

automationPlan: Automate release metadata and artwork variants
Mailing-list announcements via Bandcamp/Email API
Schedule promo posts around Bandcamp Fridays
risks: Needs an audience; discovery is limited
Ownership changes (Songtradr acquired Bandcamp in 2023) could alter terms
Bandcamp Fridays are confirmed only through Dec 2026
evidence: Bandcamp's help center publishes its revenue-share schedule; it has been a primary direct-sales channel for independent musicians for over a decade.

skills: building a fan community on social media/email

unitEconomics.notes: Album prices of $5-20 (fans often pay above minimum); Bandcamp keeps 15% on digital (10% after $5k in 12 months) and processors take a further 4-6% (cost rounded up to $1).

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash outlay; first sale comes from friends and existing fans, often within the first Bandcamp Friday.

marketConditions.notes: Bandcamp works for artists who already have fans in niche genres; discovery for unknowns is weak. Bandcamp Fridays continue through Dec 2026 and concentrate sales. Most artists sell a handful of downloads per release. Failure mode: releasing without an audience or email list.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Use name-your-price with a low minimum on singles and $7-10 on albums, add a fan subscription and bundle limited physical items for core fans.
profitPath: Month 0: page and first release (cost $0)
Month 1-2: launch on a Bandcamp Friday to your network, $20-100
Month 3-6: regular releases, email list, subscription tier; $20-80/month
Month 6-12: merch bundles; most earn under $100/month

name: Sell sheet music and licensed arrangements via ArrangeMe (Hal Leonard) and Musicnotes
summary: Publish originals, public-domain arrangements and licensed arrangements of popular copyrighted songs as sheet music sold across Hal Leonard's network.
howItWorks: You arrange songs for specific instruments/levels (easy piano, string quartet, SATB) in notation software and upload PDFs or interactive scores to ArrangeMe, which clears copyrighted songs from its approved list and distributes to Sheet Music Plus, Sheet Music Direct, MuseScore and partner retailers. Teachers, students and ensembles buy them. Musicnotes Marketplace is a parallel channel. AI transcription tools speed up drafts but humans must check notation.

payout.notes: Verified from ArrangeMe Terms: originals/public-domain arrangements 50% (52% Pro), copyrighted arrangements 10% (12% Pro) on Hal Leonard sites; 70% of receipts for subscriptions/extended network. Paid ~30 days after month end. Musicnotes Marketplace (help center): free Creator membership allows up to 10 uploaded arrangements (paid tiers for more); copyrighted songs must be on Musicnotes' licensed list; royalties are auto-calculated by song classification, but the rates are not published in the help center.

legality.notes: Legal: ArrangeMe obtains licenses for approved copyrighted songs; arranging unlicensed copyrighted songs outside such programs infringes copyright.
complianceRequirements: only arrange songs on the approved list or public domain/originals

availability.notes: ArrangeMe accepts sellers internationally; PayPal payout. PayPal receiving is limited in a few reference countries (e.g. Bangladesh, Libya, Iraq); Payoneer/Wise or local alternatives may be needed.

automationPlan: Use AI audio-to-MIDI/notation tools for first drafts
Script PDF generation, titling, difficulty tags and descriptions
Track best-selling songs/levels to choose next arrangements
evidence: ArrangeMe's published terms specify commission rates, $20 PayPal threshold and monthly payment; it is Hal Leonard's official self-publishing channel.

skills: arranging for specific instruments and levels

unitEconomics.notes: Hal Leonard sites list single arrangements at about $4-8. ArrangeMe pays 50% on originals/public-domain (fee 50%) but only 10% on copyrighted arrangements. Hours amortise arranging over expected sales.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash outlay; the $20 PayPal minimum and month-end-plus-30-day lag push first cash to month 3-6.

marketConditions.notes: Sellers with large catalogues of easy-level arrangements of popular or seasonal songs earn steadily; single arrangements rarely sell. Copyrighted pop titles sell more but pay only 10%. AI transcription speeds drafting but also adds supply. Failure modes: tiny catalogue, competition with free MuseScore scores.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Price at the default $5-6 for single parts, slightly more for ensemble scores; build volume across 50+ titles and seasonal pieces rather than raising prices.
profitPath: Month 0: first 10 arrangements uploaded (cost $0)
Month 1-3: first sales, first payout once $20 accrues
Month 3-6: 30-50 titles, seasonal content; $20-60/month
Month 6-12: 80-100 titles; most earn $30-150/month

name: Collect songwriter publishing royalties (PRO registration, The MLC, Songtrust, live-performance reporting)
summary: Register your compositions with a performing-rights organization, The MLC and/or a publishing administrator to collect performance and mechanical royalties that distributors do not pay.
howItWorks: Streaming distributors pay only master royalties; the composition side (performance and mechanical) is collected by PROs (ASCAP/BMI/PRS/SOCAN etc.), The MLC for US streaming mechanicals, or an admin like Songtrust worldwide. You register songs, splits and ISWCs, and report live and livestreamed setlists through PRO online performance-reporting programs. Money that would otherwise go unclaimed flows to you.
platforms: ASCAP / BMI / PRS for Music / local PRO

payout.minimumPayout: PRS: £30 (UK) / £60 (international); The MLC pays monthly; others vary by society
payout.notes: Verified: The MLC is free and distributes monthly; Songtrust charges a one-time $100 fee plus 15% of performance / 20% of mechanical royalties. ASCAP is free to join as a writer, and ASCAP OnStage pays royalties for live sets at ASCAP-licensed venues, with claims due one quarter after the performance quarter (classical/recital and non-licensable events are excluded); payment by direct deposit. PRS for Music charges a one-off £100 joining fee (£30 under 25; MCPS is a separate £100), pays once earnings exceed £30 UK / £60 international, and lets members register live performances in the dashboard. BMI fees and BMI Live rules could not be fetched (bmi.com returned 403); livestream eligibility under OnStage is not stated.

legality.notes: Collective rights management is legal in all reference countries; most have a national CMO, though local societies vary in efficiency.
complianceRequirements: PRS has a £100 joining fee; ASCAP and The MLC are free

availability.notes: Every reference country has access to at least one PRO (local or foreign); The MLC accepts anyone owed US mechanicals. Payout is direct deposit to bank.

automationPlan: Script bulk song registration data (titles, ISRC/ISWC, splits)
Scheduled matching checks of unclaimed works
Automate setlist submissions after streams/gigs
evidence: The MLC distributes monthly; ASCAP says it is free to join as a writer and pays OnStage live-performance royalties; PRS paid out £1.07bn in 2025, with nearly 7,000 members paid for the first time.

tools: PRO member portal (ASCAP/BMI free; PRS GBP 100)

unitEconomics.notes: Composition royalties are roughly $0.0003-0.0008 per stream combined (estimate); figures assume direct PRO/MLC registration (Songtrust would take 15-20%).

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash if you choose free PROs (PRS charges GBP 100). Royalties lag 6-12 months behind plays.

marketConditions.notes: This only captures money your music already earns; it pays meaningfully only for catalogues with hundreds of thousands of streams or regular live performances. US mechanical rates are rising under Phonorecords IV, but AI-generated tracks dilute streaming pools. Failure modes: tiny catalogues earning cents, mis-registered splits.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: No pricing; maximise by registering every song in every relevant society and reporting every live set.
profitPath: Month 0: join a PRO and The MLC, register catalogue (cost $0)
Month 1-6: report live sets and fix registrations; no payments yet
Month 6-9: first statements, often under $10
Month 9-12: steady small monthly MLC and quarterly PRO payments

name: Direct-upload platform monetization on SoundCloud and Audiomack
summary: Upload music directly to SoundCloud (paid Artist/Artist Pro plan, fan-powered royalties, 100% royalty share) or Audiomack (AMP monetization program) and earn per-listener royalties.
howItWorks: Unlike DSP distribution, these platforms let you upload directly and monetize on-platform plays. SoundCloud pays fan-powered royalties (based on each listener's actual listening time and the ad/subscription revenue they generate) on tracks monetized through a paid Artist or Artist Pro subscription; there is no minimum-stream requirement and approval takes about 5 business days. Audiomack's AMP is free for authenticated artists with 100+ followers and 50K plays in 6 months, or available immediately with an Audiomack Pro subscription; it is popular in Africa and the Caribbean. Only 100% original, fully owned music qualifies on both. You grow plays through reposts, playlists and community engagement.

payout.minimumPayout: SoundCloud: $25 (after processing fees, from $0.50); Audiomack: not published
payout.frequency: monthly (SoundCloud, last business day; Audiomack NET 90)
payout.notes: Verified (help centers, Nov 2026): SoundCloud monetization requires a paid Artist (2 monetized tracks/month, select territories) or Artist Pro (unlimited) plan; artists keep 100% of royalties since Nov 2025; payouts go to PayPal or bank once the balance reaches $25, about two months in arrears (first data after 45-60 days). Audiomack AMP: free entry needs an authenticated profile, 100 followers and 50K plays in the last 6 months, or an Audiomack Pro subscription; earnings post to balance about 90 days after month end; tracks with leased beats, uncleared samples or remixes are excluded. Plan prices and Audiomack's cash-out minimum/method are not published in the help centers.

legality.notes: Legal; only upload music you own or control. Fake streams/bots violate ToS.
complianceRequirements: own 100% of rights to monetized uploads (no leased beats or uncleared samples)

availability.notes: Audiomack lists all 50 reference countries as AMP territories. SoundCloud's Artist plan is only in select territories, and SoundCloud's monetization country list was not found; it pays to PayPal or bank. PayPal receiving is limited in a few reference countries (e.g. Bangladesh, Libya, Iraq).

automationPlan: Scheduled uploads and metadata via API
LLM-generated descriptions and tags
Analytics monitoring scripts
risks: Tiny per-play payouts; SoundCloud's $25 threshold may take months to reach
SoundCloud needs a paid plan; Audiomack's free route needs 50K plays in 6 months
evidence: SoundCloud's help center documents fan-powered royalties, a 100% royalty share, a $25 threshold and monthly payouts; Audiomack's help center documents AMP eligibility, its NET 90 schedule and its territory list.

tools: SoundCloud Artist plan (~$3/mo, price not published in help center)

unitEconomics.notes: Per-play rates are not published; $5-30 per 10k plays is an estimate (Audiomack at the low end, SoundCloud fan-powered at the high end). SoundCloud artists keep 100% since Nov 2025. Hours are promotion time. Artist plan price (~$3/mo) is estimated: SoundCloud's pricing and help pages could not be fetched.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurring $3/mo (startup cash not amortised). About 2,000 SoundCloud plays a month cover the Artist plan; few new artists reach that, and payouts start at a $25 balance about two months in arrears.

marketConditions.notes: Monetized plays pay fractions of a cent, so only artists with sizeable followings earn noticeable money; Audiomack is strongest in Africa and the Caribbean. AI-generated uploads flood both platforms. Failure modes: paying the plan without enough plays and AMP thresholds not reached.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: No pricing; use the cheapest Artist tier only once plays justify it and route listeners to higher-value channels (Bandcamp, merch, live).
profitPath: Month 0: upload catalogue, subscribe to Artist plan (cost $3/mo)
Month 1-3: weekly releases and repost groups; under $5/month
Month 3-6: reach $25 cumulative balance for first payout
Month 6-12: most stay under $20/month; growth comes from a breakout track

name: Custom songs, jingles and podcast/radio intros to order
summary: Write and produce personalized songs (gifts, weddings) and short brand jingles, podcast intros and radio-style imaging for paying clients.
howItWorks: Consumers commission personalized songs for birthdays and weddings through marketplaces (e.g. Fiverr's music categories, Songfinch artist roster), and small businesses and podcasters buy jingles, sonic logos and intros. You take a brief, write lyrics (LLM-assisted drafts), record and deliver a mixed track with a usage license. Short formats make turnaround fast.

payout.notes: Fiverr: 20% fee, 14-day clearance (verified). Songfinch (help center): artists set their own prices and Songfinch says it works with 'thousands of independent artists worldwide', but the artist revenue share, payout method and artist application terms are not public (the main site returns 403).

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; taxable. Do not imitate a specific artist's voice or reuse copyrighted melodies/lyrics.
complianceRequirements: no voice cloning of real artists without consent

availability.notes: Fiverr/Upwork pay out almost everywhere via Payoneer. Songfinch says its roster is worldwide, but how it pays non-US artists is not published.

automationPlan: LLM-drafted lyrics from client questionnaire
Template arrangements per style
Automated delivery packaging and license PDF
risks: AI song generators undercut low-end prices
evidence: Personalized-song and jingle gigs are long-standing Fiverr music categories with visible completed-order counts; Fiverr's fee and clearance terms are documented.

unitEconomics.notes: Fiverr custom songs typically $50-300; business jingles and sonic logos $200-600+. Fiverr fee 20%; cost covers sample/AI credits.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash outlay; first order usually within 1-2 months of listing with samples.

marketConditions.notes: Personalised songs for weddings and birthdays and podcast intros remain popular gifts and needs, but AI song generators now produce a passable personalised song for under $10, squeezing the low end. Human vocals, real storytelling and fast delivery still sell at $100+. Failure modes: price competition and buyers switching to AI tools. Fact-check: median month-12 net lowered from $200 to $70 so it agrees with the 30% profit likelihood (fewer than half of starters clear $100/month, so the median starter cannot).

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Start with a $50-80 package (60-second song, 3-day delivery) to get reviews, then raise to $150+ and sell add-ons (full length, instrumental, rush).
profitPath: Month 0: 3 sample songs and gig listings (cost $0)
Month 1-2: first 2-3 orders, $100-200
Month 3-6: seasonal peaks (Valentine's, weddings) plus business jingles; $200-600/month
Month 6-12: higher tiers and direct clients; $300-1,500/month for active sellers

name: Get paid as a music curator to review submissions (SubmitHub, Groover)
summary: Owners of music blogs, playlists, radio shows or channels get paid per submission to listen and give written feedback, without being paid for placement.
howItWorks: Artists pay platforms like SubmitHub and Groover to send tracks to curators. Approved curators must listen and respond with feedback within a deadline; they are paid per reviewed premium submission whether or not they accept the song. Payment is for listening/feedback, not guaranteed placement, which keeps it within platform rules and anti-payola norms. Requires first building a real outlet with an audience to be accepted.

payout.minimumPayout: Groover: €20 first withdrawal, then €50; SubmitHub: not published
payout.frequency: on request (Groover: one free withdrawal per 30 days)
payout.notes: Groover (help center): Grooviz withdraw by Wise bank transfer (IBAN/local; some territories such as Brazil and India may be restricted) or PayPal; minimum €20 for the first request, then €50; processed within 72 working hours; one free withdrawal per 30 days, then €2 each, plus a fixed €2 PayPal fee. SubmitHub curators cash out to a PayPal email (in-app). Per-review earnings for both platforms are not published, and SubmitHub's minimum is unknown. Unconfirmed: SubmitHub's curator cash-out minimum and fees (submithub.com/apply and /help do not state them).

legality.notes: Legal; paid review is permitted when no placement is guaranteed. Placements in exchange for money would breach platform rules and DSP playlist policies.

availability.notes: Both platforms accept curators internationally by application. Groover pays by Wise (some territories, e.g. Brazil and India, may be restricted) or PayPal; SubmitHub pays by PayPal only. PayPal receiving is limited in a few reference countries (e.g. Bangladesh, Libya, Iraq).

automationPlan: LLM-assisted drafting of feedback from your listening notes
Queue triage scripts by genre
Automated publishing of accepted tracks to blog/playlist
risks: Low-effort AI-only feedback gets curators removed
Fake playlist followers lead to bans
evidence: Groover's help center documents curator Grooviz withdrawals to bank or PayPal and curator acceptance criteria; SubmitHub's app offers PayPal cash-outs to curators. Per-review rates are unpublished.

skills: building a real audience for a music outlet

unitEconomics.notes: Curator pay per review is not published; about $0.50-1.50 per review is an estimate from curator reports. Figures are already net of the platform's share. Estimated; Groover confirms a EUR 20 first withdrawal minimum (EUR 50 after), but neither Groover nor SubmitHub publishes per-review pay.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash outlay, but you need an established outlet before approval; Groover's first withdrawal needs EUR 20.

marketConditions.notes: Indie artists keep paying for feedback and playlist consideration, and curators with real, engaged audiences get the most submissions. Platforms remove curators with fake or inactive outlets. Failure modes: rejection as a curator and too few submissions to matter.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Accept the platform's default price at first, keep response times fast to rise in rankings, then raise your credit price as acceptance quality builds a reputation.
profitPath: Month 0-3: grow a playlist/blog/channel to a real audience (cost $0)
Month 3-4: apply to SubmitHub and Groover
Month 4-6: 50-100 reviews/month, $40-100/month
Month 6-12: higher pricing and more outlets; most earn $50-200/month

name: Paid music and product reviewing on Slicethepie
summary: Listen to unreleased songs (and review fashion/video items) and get paid small amounts per written review.
howItWorks: Slicethepie plays you a track clip and you write a short critique and rating; better-quality reviews raise your star rating and per-review pay. Labels and brands use aggregated listener feedback for market research. Pay per review is small but available with no audience or skills.

payout.notes: Verified (terms and FAQ): $20 minimum withdrawal; once your balance reaches $50 you are required to withdraw, and accounts reaching $100 unwithdrawn are locked and archived. Payouts go to PayPal (email must match the account) or Revolut (fee-free, verified by a $0.01 test payment), with Airtm and gift cards listed on the homepage for some regions. Pay per review depends on star rating and is not published.

legality.notes: Legal market-research activity; reviews must be genuine opinions written by you.

availability.notes: Open to reviewers worldwide subject to panel geo requirements; PayPal/Revolut/Airtm cover most reference countries.

automationPlan: Track earnings and auto-remind to withdraw before the $50 prompt and $100 lock
manualSteps: Listening and writing each review yourself (automation would violate ToS)
risks: Review quality scoring can reduce pay
Account locked if the balance reaches $100 unwithdrawn
evidence: Slicethepie's FAQ says over 10 million reviews have been submitted and more than $1 million paid to reviewers; its terms set a $20 minimum threshold.

skills: writing short, specific music critiques in English

unitEconomics.notes: Per-review pay is not published; $1-4/hour is an estimate from user reports and rises with star rating.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash; first $20 withdrawal takes about 10-20 hours of reviewing.

marketConditions.notes: Payment is near-certain for anyone who keeps reviewing, but pay is far below minimum wage and the entry's own ceiling (~$40/month) means $100/month net is out of reach; the likelihood here reflects reaching steady small profit, like survey panels. Low-effort or AI-written reviews lower your rating and pay.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: No pricing; raise per-review pay by writing detailed reviews to climb the star rating.
profitPath: Month 0: sign up, first reviews (cost $0)
Month 1-2: reach $20 and withdraw via PayPal/Revolut
Month 3-12: $10-40/month in spare time; withdraw before $50 to avoid lockout

name: Music transcription to sheet music/tabs/MIDI for clients
summary: Convert recordings or demos into notated sheet music, guitar tabs, lead sheets or MIDI for songwriters, students and bands.
howItWorks: Clients send audio of their own songs or performances and you deliver notation (MuseScore/Sibelius/Dorico files, PDF, Guitar Pro tabs) or MIDI. AI audio-to-notation tools produce a first draft; you correct rhythm, voicing and layout. Buyers include songwriters registering works, teachers, worship bands and players who need lead sheets.

legality.notes: Legal for the client's own or public-domain works. Selling transcriptions of copyrighted songs to third parties requires a license; for client private use, rules vary by country.
complianceRequirements: transcribe only works the client owns/controls or public domain, or for private study

availability.notes: Fiverr/Upwork pay out almost everywhere via Payoneer. PayPal receiving is limited in a few reference countries (e.g. Bangladesh, Libya, Iraq); Payoneer/Wise or local alternatives may be needed.

automationPlan: AI audio-to-MIDI/notation draft (e.g. stem separation + pitch tracking)
Scripted export to PDF/MusicXML/GP formats
Template intake forms
risks: AI tools reduce willingness to pay for simple transcriptions
evidence: Music transcription is an established Fiverr/Upwork service category; Fiverr's fees and clearance are documented.

unitEconomics.notes: Fiverr transcription gigs run $20-150 per song depending on length and instruments; Fiverr fee 20%; cost is AI tool credits.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash outlay; first order typically within 1-2 months.

marketConditions.notes: Songwriters, teachers and church bands keep ordering lead sheets and tabs, and transcribers who deliver clean engraving quickly get repeat work. AI audio-to-notation drafts are now good enough for simple songs, lowering prices at the basic end; complex multi-part scores still need humans. Failure modes: rhythm errors and underpricing hours of work. Fact-check: median month-12 net lowered from $150 to $60 so it agrees with the 30% profit likelihood (fewer than half of starters clear $100/month, so the median starter cannot).

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Price per minute of audio and per instrument, starting around $20-30 for a simple lead sheet; raise after 10 reviews and charge extra for full scores and fast delivery.
profitPath: Month 0: 3 sample transcriptions and gigs (cost $0)
Month 1-2: first 3-5 orders, $100-200
Month 3-6: repeat clients; $200-500/month
Month 6-12: full scores and direct clients; $300-1,000/month for active sellers
